images.title: 44 is a multiple of each of its factors
images.purpose: Show the arrays of 44 tiles as three multiplications and name the six factors, so that 44 is seen as a multiple of each of them.
images.composition: Three arrays of 44 tiles in three bands, each with its multiplication, and two lines at the bottom naming the factors and the multiple.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. At the top, centred at x 728 and y 60, the heading Arrays of 44 tiles in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (44 px). Below it exactly 3 arrays of square tiles, 44 tiles in each (132 tiles in all), every tile 22 by 22 px with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline and 4 px between tiles. ARRAY 1: 1 row of 44 tiles, filled teal #0072B2, x 100 to 1240 and y 140 to 162; under it, left aligned at x 100 and y 215, the text 1 × 44 = 44. ARRAY 2: 2 rows of 22 tiles, filled amber #E69F00, x 100 to 668 and y 280 to 328; to its right, left aligned at x 720 and y 304, the text 2 × 22 = 44. ARRAY 3: 4 rows of 11 tiles, filled reddish purple #CC79A7, x 100 to 382 and y 400 to 500; to its right, left aligned at x 430 and y 450, the text 4 × 11 = 44. All three multiplication texts are dark #1F2937 bold (40 px). At the bottom, centred at x 728, two lines of bold dark text: Factors of 44: 1, 2, 4, 11, 22, 44 at y 640 (50 px) and 44 is a multiple of each of them at y 720 (40 px). No other text and no numbers inside the tiles. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: Each multiplication that makes 44 shows that 44 is a multiple of its two factors, including 1 and 44 itself.
images.description: The arrays of 44 tiles written as 1 × 44, 2 × 22 and 4 × 11, with the factors 1, 2, 4, 11, 22 and 44 listed.
images.context: Concept image for A Number Is a Multiple of Its Factors. It follows the idea of the arrays and the multiplication lines for 12 in your maths book and uses this concept's own example, 44.
images.teaching_notes: Read each line two ways: 4 × 11 = 44 says 4 and 11 are factors, and also that 44 is a multiple of 4 and of 11. The slip to watch is leaving out 1 and the number itself.

image_decisions.why: The three arrays of 44 turn each multiplication into a statement that 44 is a multiple of both numbers.
